UK ETS technical guidance: Monitoring and Reporting Regulation 2018
current MRR technical-guidance inventory including UKETS01 general guidance
Department for Energy Security and Net Zero
UKETS01 MRR - General guidance for installations
Article 13 simplified monitoring-plan eligibility and transferred/inherent CO2, N2O and CCS monitoring boundaries
controls: TRANSFERRED_CO2_SUBTRACTION_RECEIVER_GATE
Almost pure fossil CO2 is transferred out rather than emitted
Subtract it from originating-installation emissions only when the receiving destination meets an Article 49 eligible route.
Subtracting transferred CO2 sent to an ineligible destination
PASS
TRANSFERRED_CO2_CAPTURE_DESTINATION_ELIGIBLE
Transferred CO2 goes to a capture installation for transport and long-term geological storage
Treat the destination as eligible only when the storage chain is permitted under the CCS licensing regime.
Crediting an unqualified capture destination
PASS
TRANSFERRED_CO2_TRANSPORT_NETWORK_DESTINATION_ELIGIBLE
Transferred CO2 goes to a transport network for long-term geological storage
Treat the destination as eligible when linked to a storage site permitted under the CCS licensing regime.
Subtracting CO2 sent to a non-storage transport route
PASS
TRANSFERRED_CO2_STORAGE_DESTINATION_ELIGIBLE
Transferred CO2 goes to a geological storage site
Require a storage site permitted under the CCS licensing regime for long-term geological storage.
Subtracting CO2 sent to an unpermitted storage destination
PASS
TRANSFERRED_CO2_PCC_DESTINATION_ELIGIBLE
Transferred CO2 goes to precipitated calcium carbonate production
Allow the specific route only where the used CO2 is chemically bound in PCC.
Treating any product use as permanent CO2 binding
PASS
TRANSFERRED_CO2_OTHER_DESTINATION_COUNTS_ORIGIN
Transferred CO2 goes to a destination outside the eligible Article 49 routes
Count the transferred CO2 as an emission of the originating installation.
Creating an emissions deduction from ordinary CO2 transfer
PASS
PCC_CALCULATION_BASED_METHOD_GATE
CO2 is transferred for PCC production
Use the required calculation-based approach to determine eligible chemically bound CO2.
Using an unsupported measurement-only deduction for PCC
PASS
PCC_BOUND_CO2_STOICHIOMETRIC_DETERMINATION
The PCC route is used
Determine the amount of CO2 chemically bound using the applicable stoichiometric relationship and supporting monitoring data.
Deducting total CO2 delivered rather than the amount demonstrably bound
PASS
PCC_ACCESS_MONITORING_VERIFIER_GATE
Relevant PCC monitoring is performed at a receiving installation
Ensure the necessary monitoring access and verifier access are available to substantiate the bound amount.
Claiming a deduction that cannot be independently checked
PASS
PCC_TOTAL_TRANSFER_NOT_EQUAL_BOUND_AMOUNT
CO2 is supplied to a PCC producer
Do not equate total transferred CO2 with the deductible amount; determine the quantity actually bound.
Overstating the deduction by assuming all delivered CO2 is fixed in PCC
PASS
CCS_CHAIN_RECEIVER_ADD_BEFORE_RETRANSFER
A CCS installation receives transferred CO2 and later transfers CO2 onward
Add received CO2 into the receiving installation accounting before subtracting the amount transferred to the next eligible installation.
Losing CO2 between successive CCS-chain installations
PASS
CCS_TRANSFER_POINT_CONTINUOUS_MEASUREMENT
CO2 crosses transfer points in a CCS chain
Monitor relevant entering or leaving CO2 at transfer points using appropriate continuous measurement systems.
Unmeasured custody transfer within a CCS chain
PASS
CCS_CMS_CEMS_RULESET_GATE
Continuous measurement systems are used at CCS transfer points
Apply the relevant CEMS measurement-quality rules to the transfer-point systems.
Using lower-quality transfer metering without the applicable QA framework
PASS
CCS_TRANSFER_TIER4_DEFAULT
A CCS transfer-point measurement tier is selected
Use the highest tier, tier 4, unless unreasonable costs or technical infeasibility are demonstrated.
Normalising avoidable lower-tier CCS transfer measurement
PASS
CCS_TRANSFER_PARTY_IDENTIFIER_GATE
Transferred CO2 is reported between installations
Clearly identify transferring and receiving installations using the unique identifiers used in the UK ETS Registry.
Creating transfer records that cannot be reconciled across installations
PASS
CCS_INTERFACE_METER_OWNER_CHOICE
A transfer interface is monitored
Allow measurement by either the transferring or receiving installation, provided the approved monitoring arrangement is clear.
Assuming both parties must independently meter every transfer
PASS
CCS_DUAL_MEASUREMENT_ARITHMETIC_MEAN
Both transferring and receiving installations measure the same transfer and results differ within acceptable uncertainty
Use the arithmetic mean as specified.
Selecting the more favourable of two custody-transfer results
PASS
CCS_DUAL_MEASUREMENT_EXCESS_DEVIATION_GATE
Dual transfer measurements differ by more than the uncertainty approved in the monitoring plan
Use a conservative adjusted value requiring regulator approval.
Averaging materially inconsistent meters without escalation
PASS
CO2_TRANSPORT_NETWORK_ANCILLARY_SCOPE
A CO2 transport network is defined
Include functionally connected ancillary plant such as booster stations and heaters in the transport-network scope.
Excluding connected transport emissions from the boundary
PASS
CO2_TRANSPORT_OWN_ACTIVITY_SEPARATE
A transport network has fuel or ancillary operational emissions
Monitor own-activity emissions separately from losses of transported CO2.
Mixing combustion emissions with pipeline CO2 losses
PASS
CO2_TRANSPORT_VENT_LEAK_FUGITIVE_SCOPE
A CO2 transport network is monitored
Include venting, leakage and fugitive emissions from transported CO2.
Ignoring non-combustion losses from the transport network
PASS
CO2_TRANSPORT_METHOD_A_OR_B_GATE
Transported-CO2 losses are quantified
Use one of the recognised Annex IV routes: overall mass balance Method A or individual-source Method B.
Inventing an unsupported hybrid loss methodology
PASS
CO2_TRANSPORT_METHOD_A_INPUT_OUTPUT_BALANCE
Method A is used
Calculate losses from the measurement-based balance of CO2 entering and leaving the transport network.
Estimating Method A losses without complete transfer-point quantities
PASS
CO2_TRANSPORT_METHOD_B_ALL_RELEVANT_SOURCES
Method B is used
Monitor all relevant vented, leaked and fugitive release sources.
Applying Method B to only the easiest loss points
PASS
CO2_TRANSPORT_METHOD_B_7_5_UNCERTAINTY_GATE
Method B is used
Demonstrate to the regulator that overall uncertainty for CO2 emitted from the transport network does not exceed 7.5%.
Using Method B without the required overall uncertainty evidence
PASS
CO2_TRANSPORT_METHOD_B_NO_TRANSFER_ADD_SUBTRACT
Method B is used
Do not add received CO2 to or subtract transferred CO2 from the Method B emissions total as prohibited for that route.
Double counting transfer quantities within source-by-source loss accounting
PASS
CO2_TRANSPORT_METHOD_B_ANNUAL_METHOD_A_VALIDATION
Method B is the primary transport-loss method
Validate Method B with Method A at least once annually; lower tiers may be used for the validation.
Leaving individual-source loss estimates without periodic mass-balance reconciliation
PASS
CO2_STORAGE_LEAK_SOURCE_ADD_WHEN_DETECTED
A leak from the geological storage complex is detected
Add the leak as an emission source in the monitoring plan and monitor it under the applicable storage rules.
Failing to activate monitoring after a detected storage leak
PASS
CO2_STORAGE_LEAK_SOURCE_REMOVE_AFTER_NO_LONGER_DETECTED
A previously detected storage leak can no longer be detected
The related leak source may be removed from the monitoring plan and no longer monitored or reported under that leak source.
Continuing a leak source indefinitely without the condition that triggered it
PASS
CO2_STORAGE_INJECTION_VENT_FUGITIVE_SCOPE
CO2 is injected for geological storage
Monitor vented and fugitive emissions associated with injection under the applicable Annex IV rules.
Ignoring surface releases from storage injection operations
PASS
CO2_STORAGE_ANCILLARY_INSTALLATION_SCOPE
Ancillary facilities are functionally connected to the storage complex
Monitor facilities such as intermediate storage, booster, liquefaction, gasification, purification stations or heaters as applicable UK ETS installation sources.
Excluding connected ancillary emissions from storage-site accounting
PASS
TRANSFERRED_N2O_RECEIVER_MRR_GATE
N2O is transferred to another installation and the origin seeks to subtract it
Require the receiving installation to monitor and report under the MRR.
Subtracting N2O transferred outside the regulated monitoring chain
PASS
TRANSFERRED_N2O_RECEIVER_TREAT_AS_GENERATED
An eligible receiving installation receives transferred N2O
Treat the N2O as if generated within the receiving installation, including applicable CEMS monitoring and reporting.
Losing transferred N2O from both installations' reports
PASS
TRANSFERRED_N2O_NO_USE_OR_DESTRUCTION_ORIGIN_COUNTS
Transferred N2O is not used in the receiving installation and there is no evidence of destruction by relevant abatement
Count it as an emission of the originating installation.
Crediting an N2O transfer that merely postpones release
PASS
INHERENT_CO2_SOURCE_STREAM_FACTOR_GATE
A source stream contains inherent CO2
Include inherent CO2 in the emission factor or carbon content so it is reported by the installation that emits it.
Ignoring CO2 already present in a fuel or process gas
PASS
INHERENT_CO2_NON_ETS_TRANSFER_EXCEPTION
Inherent CO2 is transferred from a UK ETS installation to a non-ETS installation
Count that inherent CO2 as an emission of the transferring UK ETS installation rather than subtracting it.
Moving inherent CO2 outside the scheme boundary to avoid reporting
PASS
